newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Mugabe Cyprus trip costs airline money - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mugabe Cyprus trip costs airline money - paper.

text.p: Air Zimbabwe lost almost Z$1 million (US$92,000) this week after it flew two empty planes to and from Cyprus for President Robert Mugabe's state visit, the Zimbabwe Independent newspaper said on Friday.

Scores of passengers who were scheduled to fly to Nairobi were stranded in Harare on Monday because their plane was taken by Mugabe and his delegation to Cyprus, the paper quoted a senior official at the troubled national airline as saying.

Airline officials were unavailable for comment but last November a senior official who refused to be named told Reuters that each time the president travelled, flights were disrupted on Air Zimbabwe which has a shortage of planes.
The airliner returned to Zimbabwe after dropping Mugabe, his wife Grace and the rest of his entourage in Cyprus because it was needed for international flights, Zimbabwe Independent said.
The airline sent another plane to Cyprus on Wednesday to fly the presidential delegation to Italy for an official visit.
The paper quoted the airline official as saying it cost US$6,000 per hour to fly an empty plane including expenses such as fuel, overflight permits and payment to crew members.
Mugabe's frequent travels abroad have come under increasing criticism in the past year, earning him the nickname "Vasco da Gama" after the Portuguese explorer.
Political analysts say the 72-year-old president prefers to travel the world rather than tackle pressing domestic problems.
In the past 13 months Mugabe has been abroad more than 20 times with his new 31-year-old wife Grace, a former presidential secretary.
